# How Search results are born

Day 3, 13:25 · Gary Illyes, Search Relations · coverage: transcript, slides

Search features, rich results and structured data. Speaker from the next speaker's reference on stage to Gary's product rich result example; the same person as the retrieval part of Making sense of users' queries.

## Claims

- **[Stage]** Google described its search results page as an auction system in which the individual results, of different types, all bid for a place on the page; the auction is a metaphor for result types competing for space, not a reference to ads.
  <br><sub>`D3-C302` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Text results are the most common and most prominent result type on Google's results page, whether they are generated by an LLM or not, or enhanced in some other way, Google's speaker said.
  <br><sub>`D3-C303` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Which kinds of results Google shows for a query is decided by query understanding, which tries to predict the intent behind the query.
  <br><sub>`D3-C304` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) · Extends [D3-C004](../day3/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** When the query itself names the wanted result type, as 'pictures' does in 'orange pictures' (or a query asking for videos or news), Google can read the intent directly from that word.
  <br><sub>`D3-C305` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Visual Elements gallery of Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery), [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said it shows images on the web results page, not only in image search, because from 2005-2006 it saw people appending words such as 'pictures' or 'images' to their queries, which led to the launch of universal search.
  <br><sub>`D3-C306` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Used by the glossary term *Universal search*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google launched universal search on 16 May 2007, blending results from Images, Maps, Books, Video and News into its web results.
  <br><sub>`D3-C307` · Official Google Blog (16 May 2007) · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Universal search: The best answer is still the best answer](https://googleblog.blogspot.com/2007/05/universal-search-best-answer-is-still.html) · Used by the glossary term *Universal search*</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's 2007 launch post explained universal search by the growing number of separate search tools and traced it to a 2001 results-page mockup; the 2005-2006 image-seeking queries named on stage are a further motivation the post does not mention, and they predate the May 2007 launch.
  <br><sub>`D3-C308` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · [Universal search: The best answer is still the best answer](https://googleblog.blogspot.com/2007/05/universal-search-best-answer-is-still.html)</sub>

- **[Stage]** For an ambiguous query such as 'orange', Google uses historical data: it looks at how users reacted to different kinds of results for previous and similar queries and shows the result types users prefer.
  <br><sub>`D3-C309` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Automatically generating and ranking results](https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/how-search-works/ranking-results/)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's How Search Works pages say Google uses aggregated and anonymized interaction data to assess whether search results are relevant to queries, turning that data into signals for its machine-learned systems.
  <br><sub>`D3-C310` · Google Search (How Search Works) · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Automatically generating and ranking results](https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/how-search-works/ranking-results/)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google handles an image used as a search query much like a text query interpreted as an embedding: the image is broken down into vectors (embeddings) that are then searched for in the index.
  <br><sub>`D3-C311` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Extends [D2-C740](../day2/D2-S23-how-does-the-index-look-like.md) · Repeats [D1-C224](../day1/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google can still detect intent for image queries, even though they are searched as embeddings, the speaker said.
  <br><sub>`D3-C312` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google uses an abstract drawing of the search results page in its documentation so that the illustration does not go out of date as fast as a screenshot.
  <br><sub>`D3-C313` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Visual Elements gallery of Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A text result on Google's results page is made of parts such as the attribution, the title link, the snippet and the site name.
  <br><sub>`D3-C314` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Visual Elements gallery of Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Visual Elements gallery describes a text result as based on the page's textual content, with attribution, title link and snippet; attribution can include the site name, favicon and visible URL, and a rich result typically relies on structured data.
  <br><sub>`D3-C315` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Visual Elements gallery of Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google generates the parts of a text result, such as title link and snippet, from its understanding of the underlying web page, even when the site owner provides nothing extra.
  <br><sub>`D3-C316` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Influencing your title links in search results](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/title-link), [Control your snippets in search results](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/snippet) · Extends [D2-C724](../day2/D2-S23-how-does-the-index-look-like.md) · Used by `DEV-HTM-03`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google can add elements to a text result, such as a 'highly cited' badge or a preferred-source badge.
  <br><sub>`D3-C317` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Help your readers find your site through preferred sources in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/preferred-sources) · Extends [D1-C027](../day1/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Some search features work the other way round: a feature container holds text results inside it; the speaker could not recall that feature's name and suggested, unsure, linked subscriptions.
  <br><sub>`D3-C318` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Image results shown among web results come from Google's image index and are roughly the same images that Google Images shows for the same query.
  <br><sub>`D3-C319` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Extends [D2-C525](../day2/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Video results in web search have thumbnails and attribution that come from the page or from its markup.
  <br><sub>`D3-C320` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Video SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/video)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's serving diagram shows the query passing through query understanding and retrieval to the index, then back through ranking and search features to the user, with the Search Features step highlighted (example query 'Where to eat orange').
  <br><sub>`D3-C321` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) · Repeats [D3-C001](../day3/D3-S02-welcome-to-serving-and-ranking-day.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google generates search features as the last serving step: it sends the query to the index, gets results back, ranks them and then builds the search features.
  <br><sub>`D3-C322` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) · Used by the glossary term *Search features*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Most of Google's search features need nothing extra from the site owner; Google generates them from what it extracted from the page during indexing.
  <br><sub>`D3-C323` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Visual Elements gallery of Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery) · Extends [D2-C446](../day2/D2-S11-finding-the-gold-nuggets-structured-data-media-and-more.md) · Used by the glossary term *Search features*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Rich results differ from other search features because Google builds them from extra data that site owners provide, usually structured data and usually in JSON-LD format.
  > "The magic behind rich results is usually structured data. Emphasis on "usually"."
  <br><sub>`D3-C324` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Visual Elements gallery of Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery), [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data) · Extends [D2-C521](../day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) · Used by the glossary term *Rich results*, the glossary term *Search features*</sub>

- **[Stage]** AI Mode and AI Overviews are not rich results but standard search features: they need no structured data to function and work with the normal text results from Google's index.
  > "AI Mode and AI Overviews are not rich results."
  <br><sub>`D3-C325` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) · Extends [D2-C726](../day2/D2-S23-how-does-the-index-look-like.md) · Used by `DEV-AIF-02`, the glossary term *Rich results*, the glossary term *Search features*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's AI features guide says there are no additional requirements, and no special schema.org structured data, needed to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode; a page must be indexed and eligible to be shown with a snippet.
  <br><sub>`D3-C326` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) · Used by `DEV-AIF-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said that if AI Mode one day showcases images, recipes or similar elements, those parts would need structured data, but in their current form AI Mode and AI Overviews require pretty much nothing extra.
  <br><sub>`D3-C327` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Day 2 said the structured data Google processes also feeds AI Overviews and AI Mode (D2-C476), while Day 3 said these features do not need structured data to function: markup is not a condition for appearing in AI features, but data taken from it can still reach them.
  <br><sub>`D3-C328` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · Used by `DEV-AIF-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's structured data feature guide lists the kinds of structured data Google supports with a search feature and what each can do to a site's search results.
  <br><sub>`D3-C329` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Structured data markup that Google Search supports](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/search-gallery) · Repeats [D2-C490](../day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Article structured data is a broad type with many properties and nested types, which Google uses to learn more about published content, such as its headline, author and publication date.
  <br><sub>`D3-C330` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Article (Article, NewsArticle, BlogPosting) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/article) · Used by `DEV-SDA-13`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's rich results slide said Article structured data is not required to appear in Top Stories but is highly recommended for all articles.
  > "Not required for "Top Stories," but highly recommended for all articles."
  <br><sub>`D3-C331` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Article (Article, NewsArticle, BlogPosting) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/article) · Used by `DEV-SDA-13`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Article documentation says there is no markup requirement to be eligible for Google News features like Top stories, and that Article markup can tell Google more explicitly that content is a news article, who the author is and what the title is.
  <br><sub>`D3-C332` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Article (Article, NewsArticle, BlogPosting) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/article) · Used by `DEV-SDA-13`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Article rich results slide said structured data can be used to indicate that content is behind a paywall.
  <br><sub>`D3-C333` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Article (Article, NewsArticle, BlogPosting) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/article), [Structured data for subscription and paywalled content (CreativeWork)](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/paywalled-content) · Used by `DEV-SDA-13`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Article slide showed the NewsArticle JSON-LD example from Google's Article documentation: a block in the page head with headline, three image URLs (1x1, 4x3 and 16x9), datePublished and dateModified with time zone offsets, and an author list of Person objects with name and url.
  <br><sub>`D3-C334` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Article (Article, NewsArticle, BlogPosting) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/article) · Used by `DEV-SDA-13`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google described the site name as an attribution feature rather than a rich result, and said site owners can influence which site name Google shows for their site in search results.
  <br><sub>`D3-C335` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Visual Elements gallery of Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery), [Provide a site name to Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/site-names) · Used by `DEV-SDA-15`, the glossary term *Site name*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's site name documentation says site names are generated automatically from a site's home page and references to it on the web, and that a site can indicate its preferred name with WebSite structured data on its home page.
  <br><sub>`D3-C336` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Provide a site name to Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/site-names) · Used by `DEV-SDA-15`, the glossary term *Site name*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Review structured data lets a site specify how its users rated something; the review snippet shows an average star rating and often the number of reviews of a product, service or piece of content.
  <br><sub>`D3-C337` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Review snippet (Review, AggregateRating) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/review-snippet) · Extends [D2-C454](../day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) · Used by `DEV-SDA-14`, the glossary term *Review snippet*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said users rely quite a bit on review stars, calling them a powerful signal of quality and trust for users and a way for sites to use social proof to increase clicks.
  > "Those little yellow stars are a powerful signal of quality and trust for our users."
  <br><sub>`D3-C338` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Review snippets can be used for many kinds of things, from products to local businesses, movies and books.
  <br><sub>`D3-C339` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Review snippet (Review, AggregateRating) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/review-snippet) · Used by `DEV-SDA-14`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's review snippet documentation supports ratings for local businesses and organizations only on sites that capture reviews about other businesses; self-serving reviews of a site's own business are not eligible.
  <br><sub>`D3-C340` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Review snippet (Review, AggregateRating) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/review-snippet) · Used by `DEV-SDA-14`, the glossary term *Review snippet*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Some countries rely a lot on social proof such as reviews, Google's speaker said, recalling a point from Google's Day 2 internationalisation talk.
  <br><sub>`D3-C341` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Extends [D2-C614](../day2/D2-S15-focusing-on-internationalisation-and-localisation.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google called product rich results essential for any e-commerce business; they can show the product's rating, the number of reviews and other details.
  <br><sub>`D3-C342` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Introduction to Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google Search displays product rich results from product structured data; it may also use the product data a merchant provides in Google Merchant Center, but Merchant Center is not required for them.
  <br><sub>`D3-C343` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Introduction to Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product) · Used by `DEV-SHP-01`, the glossary term *Merchant Center*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Product structured data introduction says that providing both on-page structured data and a Merchant Center feed maximizes eligibility for shopping experiences and helps Google understand and verify the data; product snippets may take pricing from the feed when the markup lacks it.
  <br><sub>`D3-C344` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Introduction to Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product) · Used by `DEV-SHP-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Product annotations on Google Images results also come from product structured data and do not need Google Merchant Center.
  <br><sub>`D3-C345` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Introduction to Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product) · Used by `DEV-SHP-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** To appear in the Shopping tab of Google Search, a product must be submitted in Google Merchant Center; product structured data alone is not enough.
  <br><sub>`D3-C346` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Introduction to Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product), [Free listings for products](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9199328?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-SHP-01`, the glossary term *Merchant Center*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Merchant Center help says products and details crawled from an online store can show up on Google even when they are not marked up with schema.org or added in Merchant Center, and lists the Shopping tab among the places Merchant Center free listings appear.
  <br><sub>`D3-C347` · Google Merchant Center Help · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Free listings for products](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9199328?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's free listings help says crawled store products can appear on Google without markup or Merchant Center but does not say whether that includes the Shopping tab; for a shop that wants Shopping tab visibility, the stage rule that Merchant Center is required is the safe working assumption.
  <br><sub>`D3-C348` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · [Free listings for products](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9199328?hl=en), [Introduction to Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Product structured data can help Merchant Center in some cases, for example during data validation, but Merchant Center does not require it.
  <br><sub>`D3-C349` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Introduction to Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product), [Allow Merchant Center to update product information automatically](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-SHP-01`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Merchant Center's automatic item updates use structured data and other product data found on landing pages to fix price, sale price, availability and condition mismatches in a merchant's product data; Google says they do not replace regular feed updates.
  <br><sub>`D3-C350` · Google Merchant Center Help · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Allow Merchant Center to update product information automatically](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-SHP-01`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For an online shop, Product structured data is enough for product rich results and Google Images product annotations, but the Shopping tab needs a Merchant Center feed too; keep feed and markup values identical, since Google can use the markup to validate the feed.
  <br><sub>`D3-C351` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · Used by `DEV-SHP-01`</sub>
